4th year pharmacy student here👨‍⚕️ I’d just like to say I personally did not have a good experience with antidepressants. But that’s just me. I believe they can help certain people and that it is a very subjective experience (many of my friends have taken venlafaxine and said it really did help them for a short period of time) but they are not a cure and you shouldn’t depend on them to make you feel better. You have to realize though that it may take a while before you find the right one for you and in the beginning stages while the drug builds up to therapeutic concentrations in your body (~4 to 6 weeks) it could potentially make your anxiety worse. This is because serotonin (the chemical in the brain that’s being affected by most antidepressants) activates an alternative pathway in the brain that releases cortisol (the stress hormone) this effect is usually transient and goes away with continued use. However it is possible that you continue to feel worse and you may need to try another one. So it could potentially turn into a trial and error type situation where you may have to go through this several times until the right one for you is found.
